title: Importing a includeSubDomains parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child entry, silently drops the child. (CVE-2026-87862)
description: A vulnerability exists in the handling of HSTS policies where importing a parent domain's includeSubDomains HSTS entry before a longer-lived child domain entry causes the child entry to be silently dropped. This results in the loss of the child's valid HSTS policy when the parent expires, leading curl to downgrade to unencrypted HTTP requests instead of enforcing HTTPS.
aiSummary: The vulnerability (CVE-2026-87862) involves the processing order of HSTS entries in curl. When a parent domain's HSTS entry with includeSubDomains is imported before a child domain's longer-lived HSTS entry, the child's entry is silently discarded. Consequently, after the parent domain's HSTS policy expires, the child domain's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to fail to upgrade HTTP requests to HTTPS for that child domain.
aiImpact: The impact is that curl may issue unencrypted HTTP requests to child domains that should have enforced HTTPS due to their valid HSTS policies. This could potentially expose communications to interception or downgrade attacks if an attacker can exploit the absence of HTTPS enforcement. However, no known exploits in the wild have been reported.
